clause: The report names the instruction and the SHA
quote: A second merge is permitted only to fix a regression the live walk caught, named in the report with both SHAs, or to satisfy a mid-session instruction from the author.
reason: R-0266 requires a second merge to be named in the report with both SHAs and lists the mid-session author instruction as one of the two permitted reasons; naming the authorizing instruction and its SHA is inherent to justifying that second merge.

clause: pnpm main:green asks GitHub (the remote branch), not the working tree; four verdicts kept apart — green, red, pending, could-not-tell — a check that cannot reach its subject must never print like a passing one
quote: A check that cannot run says so. Silence is not a passing result
reason: The load-bearing obligation (a check reads server truth and a could-not-tell never prints like a pass) is carried by R-0267's 'a check that cannot run says so; silence is not a passing result' and its 'verified by command / asserts the live API' server-truth discipline. The four-verdict enumeration for main:green specifically is operational.

clause: A session may not report clean gates while leaving main failing and production stale (handoff carries a 'main checks' line, fails on RED)
quote: Status is generated, never asserted. A status claim names the gate or test that fails when it stops being true, with timestamp and SHA.
reason: Cannot-report-clean-while-main-red is carried by R-0272 (status generated not asserted; a status claim names the gate that fails) plus R-0266 ('only the integrated head ships'); production-stale is carried by R-0267 production-integrity freshness fails closed. The handoff 'main checks' line is the operational instrument of the conserved obligation.

clause: Four verdicts, cannot-tell exits non-zero; no Netlify credential is not a pass
quote: A check that cannot run says so. Silence is not a passing result
reason: The obligation (a deploy read that cannot reach its subject / lacks a credential is not a pass) is the same could-not-tell-is-not-a-pass principle carried by R-0267; protection:verify 'exits non-zero on drift and on could-not-tell' is the same verdict semantics. Deploy-specific wording is operational.

clause: Where the deploy record cannot be read, the item reports COULD_NOT_TELL and never DONE
quote: A reader-facing DONE names the production deploy that serves it — deploy id, state, and the SHA it built, read from the provider's deploy API. A deploy that never reached ready is not done.
reason: If the deploy record cannot be read, R-0266's requirement that DONE names the deploy id/state/SHA read from the API cannot be satisfied, so it cannot be DONE; R-0267's 'a check that cannot run says so' supplies the COULD_NOT_TELL verdict. Conserved by construction.

clause: PRODUCTION_RENDER remains required for activation; a STAGING_RENDER counts as INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED but never becomes the production verification and may not be recorded as one
quote: Once open, every promotion is verified on the served surface within the same window; a regression reverts the batch and opens an incident.
reason: Activation is verified on the served (production) surface (R-0268), and 'SESSION_MEASURED and INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED are distinct classes and only the latter counts toward activation'; R-0266 separates the staging render (code/schema only) from runtime civic data. A staging render therefore cannot stand as production verification.

clause: The report states the code SHA and the close-out record SHAs separately and labels them, so a reader can tell which commit changed what a reader sees
quote: Close-out records follow as separate named commits through the same gate, because a document cannot name the commit that contains it.
reason: R-0266 requires close-out records to be separate named commits distinct from the code merge; naming them separately in the record is the conserved obligation, and the 'so a reader can tell which commit changed what a reader sees' phrasing is its rationale.

clause: Not a second feature, not a second batch, not late work; any other second merge remains a deviation and is still reported as one
quote: A second merge is permitted only to fix a regression the live walk caught, named in the report with both SHAs, or to satisfy a mid-session instruction from the author.
reason: The exclusivity ('permitted only' the two reasons) is carried verbatim in substance; any other second merge is thereby unpermitted, and reporting it as a deviation is the natural consequence of the honest-reporting obligation (R-0272 status generated, never asserted; R-0273 report obligations).

clause: The check has no skip flag
quote: A session may not claim gates green unless it ran the exact gate set CI requires and named each one.
reason: The obligation (this drift check cannot be silently bypassed) is carried by R-0267's thesis 'a gate is real, or it is not a gate' plus the requirement to run the exact required set and name each; 'no skip flag' is the operational mechanism of that conserved bar (and R-0267 states 'no skip flag' outright for the scheduled pusher).

clause: There is no skip flag
quote: A session may not claim gates green unless it ran the exact gate set CI requires and named each one.
reason: pnpm gates is the required set; R-0267's requirement to run the exact CI gate set and name each, under 'a gate is real, or it is not a gate', carries the no-bypass obligation. The absence of a skip flag is the operational form.

clause: The generated journal and the files on disk must correspond exactly (a journal entry with no file, or a file with no journal entry, is a failure)
quote: A generated artifact is never hand-edited; the generator is fixed and the artifact regenerated and diffed, and a generator whose digest moved fails the build until its output is regenerated.
reason: The migration journal is a generated artifact; R-0272's regenerate-and-diff / digest-moved-fails-the-build discipline detects a journal diverging from its migration files, and its no-hand-edit rule forbids an orphan file added outside the generator. R-0267 additionally carries migration immutability.

clause: Every candidate is classified by reading it before it is wired; a pure checker may become a gate, but a mutating status/close-out/tracker writer may NOT be run as a gate merely to make a question 'covered' (a generator run as a gate would repair the staleness the gate exists to catch)
quote: No layer certifies itself, including the audit layer.
reason: A mutating generator run as a gate certifies its own freshness by producing it — the self-certification R-0274 forbids, and the same shape as R-0274's 'a suite that manufactured signal in the sold store every run would be worse than no suite'. Under R-0247 (law written once) the specific gate application is an illustration of that live principle, not a separate rule.

clause: One authoritative checker per question; a second implementation is a second verdict free to disagree with the one branch protection trusts
quote: One canonical verdict function per decision class — a model switch, for instance, is SWITCH only if every required question is measured and holds, and no second function may emit a verdict.
reason: R-0272 carries the one-authoritative-verdict-per-question rule directly ('no second function may emit a verdict'); R-0267's 'scripts/repo-path.mjs is the one implementation' is a named instance of it.

clause: The bound is an explicit parameter with no environment escape hatch and no skip flag
quote: Production-integrity freshness fails closed. A production-changing release may not proceed on an indefinitely stale healthy reading
reason: The obligation (the freshness bound cannot be bypassed by environment or skip flag) is carried by R-0267's 'fails closed' for production-integrity freshness; the explicit-parameter / no-escape-hatch wording is the operational form of failing closed.

clause: Needs Sean P1 = product is broken or fundamentally different (doesn't open / drastically changed); look now
quote: Priority is three levels, ranked inside a section and never across: P1 broken or blocking; P2 needed before the section is done; P3 wanted.
reason: The generic single scale (R-0270) carries P1 as 'broken or blocking'; 'product doesn't open / drastically changed / look now' is an illustration of that P1 meaning, applied inside Needs Sean.

clause: Needs Sean P2 = new information landed, confirm it reads right; a P2 row NAMES one body or class AND a sample size; it never says 'review the new data'
quote: A row there ends with an answerable question and the options he is choosing between; a row that cannot state one is misfiled.
reason: R-0271 requires every Needs Sean row to state an answerable/bounded question or be misfiled; a bare 'review the new data' states none and is misfiled, while naming one body/class and a sample size is the concrete form of that answerable bounding. The sample-size mechanic is operational tracker detail.

clause: Needs Sean P3 = a small adjustment, tell me if you like it
quote: Priority is three levels, ranked inside a section and never across: P1 broken or blocking; P2 needed before the section is done; P3 wanted.
reason: Generic P3 'wanted' subsumes the review-row 'small adjustment, tell me if you like it' semantics.

clause: A conditional resolution with NO condition is REFUSED (next session cannot read a blank)
quote: Conditionally resolved (condition written in plain language, binding on the next session)
reason: R-0270 defines a conditional resolution as one whose condition is written in plain language and binding on the next session; a blank condition is not that and is therefore not a valid conditional resolution. The refusal is the enforcement form of the conserved requirement that a condition must exist.

clause: Pending review — needs a look before it can close; under Needs Sean only the author reviews, under every other section a session reviews
quote: A session marks its own completed work resolved in every section except Needs Sean.
reason: The who-reviews substance survives: a session self-resolves its own completed work everywhere except Needs Sean (R-0270), and 'Only the author closes a Needs Sean row' (R-0271). The distinct 'pending review' holding state was deliberately replaced by this self-resolution model — a legitimate consolidation change, not a lost obligation.

clause: Every session reads his OPEN rows at session start (alongside the RULING 38 notes) so a row added earlier reaches the next run without a prompt mentioning it
quote: The author writes rows too, and his resolution notes are instructions, not commentary: every session opens by reading rows resolved since it last ran and treats each condition as a live requirement.
reason: The working store holds every open row (R-0270) and the session works the tracker queue; 'the author writes rows too' confirms author-added open rows sit in that queue and reach the next run unprompted. The guarantee is inherent in the tracker being the canonical queue.

clause: A session may not reword, retitle, or delete an author-written row; it may work it, set a priority if none is set, and resolve it (the description is his), enforced by a guard
restoreText: A session may not reword, retitle or delete an author-written tracker row; it may work it, set a priority if none is set, and resolve it — the row's description is the author's.
reason: R-0270 carries author-only deletion and correction-of-a-named-person-only-by-supersession, but the general bar against a session rewording or retitling the author's own (non-person) row text is carried nowhere. This is a distinct protection of author-authored content; 'the description is his' is not otherwise represented.

clause: Section edits to docs/state.md INSERT; they never replace
restoreText: Section edits to `docs/state.md` insert; they never replace, so previously recorded state is never overwritten.
reason: A distinct data-loss-prevention obligation for the standing state record (insert, never replace). No successor carries it: R-0270's append-only rule governs the tracker CSVs, not state.md, and neither R-0266's mention of 'state and log' nor R-0273's workstream-state clauses state the insert-not-replace discipline. A session could otherwise clobber recorded state.

clause: Nothing is resolved without evidence: the branch name and which of test / lint / build passed; a commit SHA cannot be used
quote: Status is generated, never asserted. A status claim names the gate or test that fails when it stops being true, with timestamp and SHA.
reason: A resolution is a status claim; R-0272 requires status to be generated and to name the gate/test behind it rather than asserted, which carries the anti-false-resolution obligation (resolve only with gate evidence). The branch-name + which-of-test/lint/build + no-bare-SHA specifics are operational tracker detail of that conserved standard.

clause: Never ask the author to paste a secret into chat, a prompt, a tracker row, a commit, a fixture or a log; a credential travels the governed secret path
quote: A credential value never reaches a transcript, log, report, commit, fixture, screenshot or evidence file, and the guard is the actual values in `.env.local`, not a pattern.
reason: R-0265 forbids a credential value reaching a transcript (chat/prompt), log, commit, fixture or evidence file regardless of source, and mandates the governed .env.local secret path — carrying both halves of the clause. A tracker row is a committed file within that scope.

clause: Each of the three numbers carries its own denominator, so the three add up to something a reader can check.
quote: Where collection and rendering can diverge, three numbers are reported: rendering, deliberately out of scope and why, and in scope and still dark.
reason: R-0254 reports exactly the three numbers as a partition (rendered / out-of-scope / in-scope-dark); each names its own scope, which is its denominator, and the partition is what makes them add up checkably. The per-number denominator is inherent in the three-way partition.

clause: Absence never wears a present value's styling: a named gap renders in the gap's own register (an outline where a recorded position renders as a filled pill), because a colour is a claim too.
restoreText: A named gap renders in the gap's own visual register, never in a present value's styling — colour and style are claims too, so an absence may not wear a recorded value's appearance.
reason: R-0254 carries the named-gap NAMING/sentence rule ('a null renders as its named gap... they never render as the same sentence') but not the styling dimension. The consolidation corpus, including the consolidation CLAUDE.md rendering lines, carries no rule that a gap's visual/colour treatment is itself a claim and must differ from a present value's. An honestly-named gap can still be styled like a filled value, so this is a distinct reader-facing honesty bar carried nowhere.

clause: One tracker row per session listing N photos, never one row per photo (else 47 candidates plus 90 officials would flood the queue).
quote: (restored separately — the photo-review tracker convention is being carried back under R-0255; repair in progress)
reason: Per the adjudication instruction, this photo-review tracker convention is already being restored separately under R-0255; recorded CONSERVED against that in-progress repair rather than re-flagged as a GAP.

clause: The contest is the unit and it is ALL-OR-NONE: every candidate in a contest is invited or none is.
quote: The questionnaire is symmetric by construction, or it is not shipped. Identical questions, word limits, deadline, reminders, and rendering of non-response.
reason: Symmetric-by-construction-or-not-shipped entails all-or-none invitation (inviting some candidates in a contest and not others is not symmetric); R-0255 also frames the contest as the unit worked 'as a unit — every candidate in it'. The invitation mechanism is operational.

clause: Nothing is ever truncated: an over-limit answer is refused at submit time with its own word count shown and the candidate decides what to cut.
quote: Answers publish verbatim and are never summarized.
reason: Verbatim-never-summarized plus identical word limits carries the anti-truncation substance (no silent shortening of an answer); the submit-time refusal with word count shown is the operational mechanism enforcing the limit without truncating.

clause: Non-response is neutral, factual and identical for everyone (invited on this date, reminded on these dates, no response yet); never evasion, avoidance, refusal or declining.
quote: Identical questions, word limits, deadline, reminders, and rendering of non-response.
reason: Identical, symmetric rendering of non-response makes it factual and forbids characterizing silence as evasion/refusal (which would also be generating a stance, barred by 'never generate a candidate position'). R-0254's named-gap rule reinforces factual non-response rendering.

clause: A withdrawal returns the candidate to the NEUTRAL INVITED STATE, never 'responded then withdrew'; renderableResponse returns the same null as an unanswered record.
quote: Every position, vote or stance carries a source record pointing at a specific statement, roll-call, filing or questionnaire response; if none exists, the field is null.
reason: A withdrawn answer is no answer on file, so the field is null (R-0255) and renders as its named gap like any non-response (R-0254); the symmetric non-response rendering forbids characterizing it as 'responded then withdrew'. The return-to-neutral-invited-state is the operational form of that null.

clause: The question set is VERSIONED and the version travels with every answer (changing it mid-cycle across candidates breaks symmetry).
quote: The questionnaire is symmetric by construction, or it is not shipped. Identical questions, word limits, deadline, reminders, and rendering of non-response.
reason: Two candidates answering different question-set versions are not answering identical questions, so they are not symmetric by construction and are not shipped; the versioning requirement is entailed by 'identical questions... or it is not shipped'. Version-travels-with-every-answer is the operational mechanism.

clause: Two clocks: certified text carries a 14-day clock, the money a 7-day clock; a presence expires as well as an absence, and one side going stale re-opens the asymmetry block automatically.
quote: Equal effort for and against is constitutional: both sides ship at equal depth or neither ships, and the check refuses rather than reports.
reason: The equal-both-sides-or-refuse check (R-0255) plus R-0250's staleness discipline ('A record that cannot say when it was measured reads as stale... stale is re-walked before it is relied on', with expiry clocks) carry 'a presence expires too and a stale side re-opens the asymmetry block': a re-walked stale side that becomes asymmetric makes the check refuse. The specific 14-day/7-day clocks are operational cadence parameters.
